neutral_facts.value: The accused and others assaulted the victim with lathis and a sword, resulting in his death at the scene. The victim's father, who was present at the incident, provided an eyewitness account. Medical evidence confirmed that the injuries were caused by sharp-edged weapons and blunt objects like lathis. The victim's father explained the delay in reporting the incident as he became unwell after his son's death. The accused were not present at the scene, but the prosecution relied on the eyewitness and medical evidence to establish their guilt. The trial court convicted the accused, and the High Court upheld the conviction for five of them, acquitting one due to his absence from the FIR.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the deceased, Partap, was mercilessly beaten and murdered by the accused appellants using weapons like lathis and swords, leading to his death. The version of the complainant, Anand Singh, was found reliable and corroborated by medical evidence. The FIR delay was satisfactorily explained as Anand Singh became unwell after his son's death.

quotes.text: The prosecution examined in all 11 witnesses. Anand Singh PW5 is the complainant. The accused abjured their guilt and contended that as Partap had tried to outrage the modesty of Monika, villagers as assembled and gave a beating to Partap due to which he died.
The version of the complainant Anand Singh-PW5 who was an eye witness to the incident has been found to be worthy of reliance.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the accused were falsely implicated in the case, as Partap had tried to outrage the modesty of Monika and was beaten by villagers. The FIR was delayed, and the prosecution failed to examine certain witnesses, which the defence claimed undermined the case against the accused.

quotes.text: It was submitted on behalf of the appellant that accused-appellants have been falsely implicated in the case. Deceased Partap had tried to outrage the modesty of Monika due to which he was beaten by the villagers.
The FIR is belated. The house of the accused was set on fire on the same day.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the version of an eye-witness, particularly a father of the deceased, is reliable if there is no motive to falsely implicate the accused and if the statement is corroborated by medical evidence.

quotes.text: The version of Anand Singh-PW5, being father of the deceased is quite reliable. He would be the last person to spare the actual assailant and would not implicate the accused falsely.

Reading of the entire statement of complainant inspired confidence and both the courts below accepted the version after full appreciation of the evidence and there were no inherent improbabilities in the version unfolded by witness.
